item.title: Naruto Sea Bream: Firm-Fleshed Prized Tai — Guide
item.description: Naruto sea bream (Naruto-dai) is some of the most highly prized tai in Japan, and its quality comes directly from the whirlpools. Living in the fast, turbulent tidal currents of the Naruto Strait, the fish must swim constantly against the powerful flow, developing exceptionally firm, lean, muscular flesh with a superb texture and clean, sweet flavour. It is at its very best in spring, the ‘cherry-blossom sea bream’ season, when the fish are plump before spawning.

item.title: Otsuka Museum of Art: Masterpieces in Ceramic — Guide
item.description: The Otsuka Museum of Art in Naruto is one of Japan’s most unusual and impressive museums: an enormous gallery displaying over a thousand of the West’s greatest artworks, all as full-size ceramic reproductions. Using a special technique, masterpieces from more than 190 galleries worldwide — the Mona Lisa, Van Gogh’s sunflowers, Monet’s water lilies, Vermeer, Munch’s Scream and countless more — are reproduced onto ceramic boards at exact original scale, faithful in colour and detail and, remarkably, near-permanent.

item.title: Sea Kayaking Around Naruto — Guide
item.description: The coast around Naruto, where the Seto Inland Sea meets the Pacific, offers scenic sea kayaking amid island scenery, quiet coves and views of the great Onaruto Bridge. Guided kayak tours let you paddle the calmer sheltered waters away from the fierce tidal race of the strait itself, gliding along the coastline, exploring inlets and small beaches, and taking in the sea and bridge from water level. Suitable for beginners with a guide, it’s a peaceful yet active way to experience the beautiful Naruto seascape up close, quite different from the roar of the whirlpools nearby.

item.title: Hyogo Nature: Mt. Rokko, Awaji Island & Coastal Trails
item.description: Hyogo Prefecture stretches across one of Japan’s most geographically diverse corridors, running from the Pacific-facing shores of the Seto Inland Sea all the way north to the dramatic cliffs and hidden beaches of the Sea of Japan coast. Between these two edges lies an interior of forested mountains, river valleys, and historic castle towns. Few Japanese prefectures can offer a visitor alpine wildflower meadows, oceanic tidal whirlpools, fishing village seascapes, and terraced rural farmland within a single day’s travel.

item.title: Tokushima Top Sightseeing: Whirlpools, Vine Bridges, and Pilgrimage Temples
item.description: Tokushima Prefecture occupies the eastern edge of Shikoku island, where tidal currents collide in one of the world’s most dramatic natural spectacles and mountain gorges hold vine bridges that have survived centuries of mountain winters. For overseas visitors, the prefecture offers an unusual combination: accessible coastal wonders near Naruto City, and remote interior landscapes that require a full day of commitment. This guide covers the five sites that should anchor any first visit.
